**Texas Tech K-12: 180-Day Course and Exam Completion Policy**

**Overview**
- For most Texas Tech K-12 online courses and Credit by Exams (CBEs), students have 180 days (six months) from the date of enrollment to complete all requirements.

**Key Points**
- **Start of 180 Days:** The countdown begins on the date you enroll in the course or exam.
- **Deadline:** All coursework, assignments, and final exams (or the CBE itself) must be completed within this 180-day window.
- **No Extensions:** Extensions beyond 180 days are not allowed. If you do not finish within this period, you must re-enroll and pay again to complete the course or exam.
- **Course Expiration:** The expiration date is posted in your student portal.

**Who Does This Apply To?**
- All students enrolled in Texas Tech K-12 online courses.
- All students taking Texas Tech K-12 Credit by Exams (CBEs).

**Additional Notes**
- For CBEs: The 180-day policy applies to both online and print versions.
- For full-time and part-time/supplemental students: The same 180-day rule applies.

**What Happens If You Don’t Finish in 180 Days?**
- You will not receive credit for incomplete work.
- You must re-enroll and pay the associated fees again if you wish to complete the course or exam.

**Reference**
- “Students have six months from the date of enrollment to complete each course. To remain in the program, students must be concurrently enrolled in a minimum of four courses.”  
- “CBEs are available for six months (180 days) after purchase. Are non-refundable and no extensions are allowed.”

**Texas Tech K-12: 180-Day Completion Policy — Part A & Part B**

**Part A: What is the 180-Day Policy?**
- Students enrolled in Texas Tech K-12 online courses or Credit by Exams (CBEs) have 180 days (six months) from the date of enrollment to complete all course requirements or the exam.
- This policy applies to both full-time and part-time/supplemental students, as well as to both online and print CBEs.

**Part B: How Does the 180-Day Policy Work?**
- **Start Date:** The 180-day period begins on the date you enroll in the course or exam.
- **End Date:** You must complete all assignments, coursework, and the final exam (or the CBE itself) within this 180-day window.
- **No Extensions:** Extensions are not available. If you do not finish within 180 days, you must re-enroll and pay again to complete the course or exam.
- **Course Expiration:** The expiration date for each course or exam is posted in your student portal.
- **Incomplete Work:** If you do not complete the course or exam within 180 days, you will not receive credit for incomplete work.

**Summary Table**

| Part | Description                                                                 |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| A    | 180 days (six months) to complete each course or CBE from enrollment date   |
| B    | No extensions; must finish all work within 180 days or re-enroll and repay  |

**Texas Tech K-12 — Student Technology Provision**

- Texas Tech K-12 does **not provide laptops or computers** to students.
- Students are required to have access to a computer that meets the minimum technology requirements for online coursework and testing.
- For the tuition-free program, families are responsible for providing a computer and reliable internet access.

**Technology Requirements:**
- Modern computer (≤5 years old) with webcam, microphone, speakers
- Windows 10+, macOS 11+, ChromeOS, or Linux (Ubuntu 18.04+)
- Reliable broadband internet
- Google Chrome (required for online exams), Firefox, Edge, or Safari (macOS only)
- Additional requirements: JavaScript enabled, cookies enabled, pop-ups allowed, ad blockers disabled

For more details on technology requirements, visit the [Technology Requirements page](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/support/handbook.php/#technology).

If you have further questions, contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.
